title: Laser printer and copier: motors, clutches, power supply, fuser lamp and scanner mirror
summary: A laser printer or copier gives 24 V brushless and stepper motors, geared drives, electromagnetic clutches and solenoids, a 24 V power supply, cooling fans, a fuser heater and a polygon-mirror laser scanner. Allow about an hour for an office machine, with a helper if it is floor-standing. The fuser stays hot for a long time and toner is a fine dust: don't breathe it, and never vacuum it with a household vacuum.

steps.text: Make it dead and cold. Switch the machine off and pull the plug from the wall. A large copier may be hard-wired or on a heavy plug: switch it off at the breaker and prove it dead (see safety_mains_isolation). Leave it at least 30 minutes, an hour for a big one, so the fuser can cool, and at least 5 minutes more for the power supply.
steps.warn: The fuser runs at around 180–200 °C and stays hot a long time after power-off.

steps.text: Deal with the toner first. Work outdoors, or in a space with doors open, on a sheet you can fold up afterwards. Wear a dust mask (N95 or P2 or better), gloves and glasses. Lift out the toner cartridges, drum units and waste-toner bottle one at a time, keep each upright and seal it in a bag. Don't open, shake or tip them.
steps.warn: Toner is a fine, combustible dust. Never vacuum it with a household vacuum, blow it with air or sweep it dry: it goes through the filter and can ignite from a motor spark. Wipe it up with a damp cloth.

steps.text: Take off the covers: paper trays, side and rear panels and the top cover. Photograph as you go. Work with the machine where it stands. On a large copier pull out one drawer at a time.
steps.warn: A floor-standing copier weighs 50–150 kg. Don't lift or tilt it (see safety_lifting).

steps.text: Fuser: at the paper exit, a metal unit with two rollers and a hot-surface sticker. Unplug its connectors, undo the 2–4 screws or levers and pull it straight out. To take the heater, remove the end holder or clip and slide the halogen lamp out of the heat roller, or lift the ceramic heater from its frame. Read the volts and watts on the lamp ends and write them down. Keep the thermistor and thermal cutout with it.
steps.warn: Check for heat with the back of your hand held near, not touching. A halogen lamp is a thin quartz tube: handle it with a cloth and don't flex it.

steps.text: Laser scanner unit: a sealed box (often under the toner area or at the top) holding the laser, a spinning polygon mirror on a motor, and lenses. Unplug its ribbon cables, undo the 3–4 screws and lift it out whole with its cover on. If you take it apart for the mirror and lenses, do it with the cables unplugged and set aside.
steps.warn: Never power the unit with its cover off, and don't look into its exit window if it could be powered. The beam is often invisible infrared.

steps.text: Motors: the brushless drive motors on the rear frame come out with 2–3 screws each and a connector. Steppers in the paper path come out the same way. Keep each gear on its shaft, bag each motor with its plug and cable, and leave encoder discs and sensors fitted.

Solenoids and clutches: these 24 V electromagnetic clutches sit on the paper feed shafts, with a coil around a toothed hub. Solenoids sit at the paper gates and pickers. Remove the E-clip or setscrew and slide each clutch off its shaft. Keep the clips in a tub.
steps.warn: E-clips and small springs fly off when released. Wear eye protection and cover the clip with a finger as you pry it.

steps.text: Power supply: a metal box or board at the rear with the mains inlet. Unplug its harnesses, undo its screws and take it whole. Read the label for the outputs (about 24 V and 5 V, and the amps).
steps.warn: Don't open it or touch its board. Its capacitors can hold a mains-level charge after unplugging (see safety_discharge_capacitor).

steps.text: Fans: each 24 V cooling fan is held by 2 screws or clips and a connector. Take them whole.
Gear trains: unscrew each gear plate or box whole so the gears stay meshed in order. Photograph it first. The rollers on steel shafts, the steel gears and the shafts are worth keeping.
Leave the high-voltage board that feeds the charge and transfer rollers, and the drum and developer units. Don't poke at the cable that leads to the roller contacts.
steps.warn: The high-voltage board makes thousands of volts at low current. A shock hurts and can throw your hand into sharp metal.

steps.text: Clean up. Wipe your work area with a damp cloth: don't sweep. Put the cloths and the sheet in a bag. Wash hands and face with cold water, because warm water melts toner into the skin, and change out of the clothes you wore.

notes:
## What's worth keeping and why

- **Brushless 24 V motors.** Quiet, efficient drive motors. They need a brushless driver, so keep the plug and the small driver board if you can. Identify them first (see skill_identify_motors, test_motor).
- **Stepper motors.** Accurate positioning for a feeder, a slider or a small machine. They need a stepper driver.
- **Clutches and solenoids.** 24 V pulse actuators for latches, gate catches and valves. A clutch engages a shaft with a 24 V coil, a simple on-off drive.
- **24 V power supply.** A good clean source of 24 V at 2–15 A for the motors and fans you took, or for a step-down converter to 12 V.
- **Fans.** 24 V fans run quiet and slower on 12 V. Use them for ventilation, a stove blower or a battery box.
- **Fuser heater.** A 400–1500 W mains heating element, rated at 120 or 240 V. Use it in a drying cabinet or a small heater only inside a metal housing, with a thermostat and a fuse. See safety_mains_isolation and test_continuity for checking the element.
- **Polygon mirror and lenses.** First-surface mirrors and long lenses for light signalling, solar projects and optics experiments.
- **Gears, shafts and rollers.** Steel and brass gears, ground steel shafts and rubber rollers for small machines.

## Variations

- Small desktop laser printers weigh 8–15 kg, with one main drive motor, a stepper and a few solenoids. The fuser and power supply are inside. Take the same parts.
- Colour laser printers have four drums, four toners, an extra belt and more motors. More toner dust: take more care.
- Large copiers carry a scanner on top with a lamp (LED, or an older xenon or cold-cathode tube), mirrors, a belt-driven carriage and heavy glass. Older cold-cathode lamps hold a little mercury: keep them whole.
- Some copiers have a small hard drive (see teardown_hard_drive).
- Inkjets are a different job (see teardown_inkjet).

## What to leave

- Toner cartridges, drums, developer, waste toner and any dusty plastic: keep sealed and away from food, children and the house.
- The high-voltage board, the drum and the developer.
- Sheet-metal frame panels, unless you need the steel.
